content: 1. GRAMMAR SPIRAL (W105 Evidence Integration): Write one complete evidence sandwich (Signal phrase + quote + citation + comment) from your research notes.

2. STRUCTURE: Label the parts: [a] 'Did you know that plastic takes 400 years to break down?' [b] 'This report will examine the causes and effects of plastic pollution.' [c] 'This report argues that plastic pollution can be significantly reduced with proper government policy.'
3. MATH SPIRAL: Your report will include data. A survey found: 40 students support plastic bans, 15 are unsure, 5 oppose. Express these as ratios (e.g., 8:3:1) and percentages.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  A research report is a structured piece of academic writing that presents findings from research. It is different from a story (narrative) because it focuses on facts, evidence, and analysis rather than a sequence of events.
content: 📖 A research report is a structured piece of academic writing that presents findings from research. It is different from a story (narrative) because it focuses on facts, evidence, and analysis rather than a sequence of events.

The structure of a research report has three main parts. The INTRODUCTION tells the reader what the report is about, why the topic is important, and what the report will cover. A good introduction has a 'hook' — an interesting fact or question — followed by background information, and finally a thesis statement: your answer to the Main Research Question.

The BODY contains multiple paragraphs, each focusing on one sub-question. Each body paragraph uses the PEEL structure: Point (main idea), Evidence (quote or paraphrase), Explanation (what the evidence means), Link (connect to the next paragraph or restate the point).
The CONCLUSION summarizes the key findings and restates the answer to the Main Question in new words.
(↑ Re-read the story above to answer:)
